A lossless copy keeps the problem, so th: A lossless copy keeps the problem, so the clips would keep jumping here (and in Chrome or Edge) even though they look fine in VLC. Repairing re-encodes the video of every clip, at full resolution, so the clips are correct everywhere. The audio is still copied without loss. Only the parts you actually cut are encoded, so this costs a few seconds per clip, not a re-encode of the whole file.
A lossless cut cannot end on an arbitrar: A lossless cut cannot end on an arbitrary frame: it stops a few frames early and drops the last B-frames. When several clips are merged, that missing piece is in the middle of the file: a short freeze at every join. A copied clip can also start a few frames late, which puts two frames on the same timestamp. A player follows the audio clock, so after you seek it re-aligns and drops frames to catch up: that is the burst of fast playback. It is a known ffmpeg limitation (see mifi/lossless-cut #2921 and #1202), not a player bug. A and B repair it by re-encoding the first and last group of frames of every clip (up to one GOP at each end, about 2-4 seconds per cut point on a source with a 4 second GOP) and by telling the merge exactly where each clip's video ends; the middle of every clip is still copied untouched. A keeps a few extra frames past every cut end, B cuts exactly where you asked. C keeps the old command line: no re-encoding at all, but the joins keep both defects. The choice applies to every cut result, a single clip included, because a result that is merged later can no longer have its ends re-encoded. The repair only works for H.264 sources without rotation; other sources, and an unknown frame rate, fall back to the old behaviour and the dialog says which rule stopped it.
A lossless cut stops before its end time: A lossless cut stops before its end time, so the last result can miss the frame you stopped on. When this is on, the last result keeps that frame; when its cut end is also the end of the video, it is extended to the source video's real last frame, even when the player reports a shorter duration (AV1 sources do this). A last result that stops before the video end keeps its cut point and only includes one more frame. Only the last result changes: the other results, the A/B/C join repair and base mode are untouched. Turn it off to keep the exact cut, without the extra frame.

The app does not delete source videos on its own. They are moved into the waiting-for-deletion folder instead.

The finish job permanently deletes only files the app created: cut results the merged result covers, or merged results you no longer need, and the like.

A source video is deleted for good only in the deletion check, on the sources you select there, and only when the app kept a result of them.

Emptying the recycle bin often to free space risks losing files other apps deleted that you may still want back:
the better way is to move files aside and delete them permanently by hand.

Moving a file into a folder, or deleting it to the recycle bin, does not free disk space.

What really frees space is permanent deletion (Shift+Delete in Explorer),

and emptying the recycle bin is permanent deletion too.

So: a source video is only moved into the waiting-for-deletion folder; deleting one for good happens only in the deletion check, from the sources that are ready there.

Reordering clips is not always a pure re: Reordering clips is not always a pure rename. A lossless cut is exclusive at its end: the frame sitting exactly at the cut point is left out. For a clip in the middle that's fine, because the next clip starts there and supplies that frame. The last clip in the export order has nothing after it, so it keeps the frame at its cut end and the merged video does not lose it. A swap that changes which clip is last therefore cuts that clip again; the rest are reused or renamed, and the merge is just a fast stream copy. A clip that reaches the end of the source is always extended to the real end, whatever its position in the order, so that extension never causes a re-cut. Your cut points and times are unchanged.
